newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU, Korea to sign trade pact on Monday.
newsitem.headline: EU, Korea to sign trade pact on Monday.

text.p: South Korea and the European Union, despite difficulties over access to Korean telecoms markets, are to sign a five-year trade agreement on Monday.
Korean Foreign Minister Gong Ro-Myung will attend an EU foreign ministers meeting in Luxembourg to sign the pact.
Under the agreement, which the EU approved in June, both sides will grant each other most-favoured nation trading status.
The pact is designed to develop trade and establish commericial, scientific and technology links between the two countries.
It is also intended to promote investment between the two.
Trade Commissioner Sir Leon Brittan is expected to raise with Gong the EU's view that it is being discriminated against in telecommunications procurement.
The Commission said on October 23 it was making a last attempt to solve the issue, hinting that it would otherwise have to take the matter to the World Trade Organisation.
Negotiations have been deadlocked since late July. The Commission blames the stalemate on a refusal by Korea to make a commitment not to interfere in bids to by private telecoms networks.
